plan: I will bid a fraction of my value in the sealed bid auction. This will allow me to stay in the ascending clock auction longer, but also risk losing the auction if the other bidders bid higher. I will bid 80% of my value, which is $40 * 0.8 = $32. This is a reasonable starting point.

My value is $13. I want to win if and only if the final price is less than $13. In the ascending clock auction, the price increases until only one bidder remains. The winner pays the price at which the second-to-last bidder exits. This price is the second-highest bid among all bidders. Therefore, to win at a price less than my value, my exit price (sealed bid) should be slightly less than my value. I will bid $12.9.

[I will bid my value. This strategy ensures that I win the auction if my value is higher than the other bidders' values, and I will not win if my value is lower. This is because in the ascending clock auction, the winner pays the second-highest bid. If my bid is my value, I will exit when the clock reaches my value. If I am the last bidder, I win at the second-highest bid, which will be less than my value. If I am not the last bidder, I lose, but I would have paid more than my value to win, so it is a good outcome.]
